---
title: "Convert gene symbols between species"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(biobouncer)
```

biobouncer does not convert an identifier from one species to another. It
guards a conversion: it cleans the symbols that go in and checks the ids that
come out. The lookup in between is done here by the
[bioclients](https://www.samuelbharti.com/bioclients/) package, which asks
IMPC for the mouse ortholog of a human gene.

This article converts a column of human gene symbols to mouse genes in three
steps:

1. Clean the human symbols.
2. Look up the mouse ortholog of each symbol.
3. Check the mouse ids that came back.

## Clean the human symbols

A lookup service can only match the symbol it is given, and a retired or
misspelled symbol may match nothing. Repair the column first. `cache` mode
checks each symbol against the HGNC snapshot that ships with the package, and
it needs no network.

```{r}
symbols <- c("TP53", "tp53", "MLL", "BRCA1", "NF1", "NOTAGENE")
res <- check_id(symbols, source_db = "hgnc", how = "cache")
res[c("input", "valid", "suggestion", "version")]
```

`tp53` has the wrong case and `MLL` is a previous symbol of `KMT2A`, so both
get a suggestion. `NOTAGENE` has none. The `version` column is the date of the
HGNC snapshot that gave the answer.

`repair_id()` applies the suggestions. Keep the symbols that are valid after
the repair, and set the others aside for a person to look at.

```{r}
clean <- repair_id(symbols, source_db = "hgnc", how = "cache")
ok <- is_valid_id(clean, source_db = "hgnc", how = "cache")

human <- unique(clean[ok])
human

clean[!ok]
```

## Look up the mouse orthologs

`impc_mouse_ortholog()` from bioclients takes one human symbol. It returns the
MGI id and the mouse symbol that IMPC holds for that gene. The call needs a
network, so the code is shown with the output of a run on 2026-11-15.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(bioclients)

lookup <- function(symbol) {
  hit <- biohttp::body_or_null(impc_mouse_ortholog(symbol))
  if (is.null(hit)) {
    hit <- data.frame(mgi = NA_character_, marker_symbol = NA_character_)
  }
  cbind(human = symbol, hit)
}

orthologs <- do.call(rbind, lapply(human, lookup))
orthologs
#>   human        mgi marker_symbol
#> 1  TP53  MGI:98834         Trp53
#> 2 KMT2A  MGI:96995         Kmt2a
#> 3 BRCA1 MGI:104537         Brca1
#> 4   NF1  MGI:97306           Nf1
```

When IMPC has no mouse ortholog for a gene, the call returns no data. The
helper turns that into a row of `NA`, so the table keeps one row per human
symbol.

## Check the mouse ids

The `mgi` source checks each id that came back.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
is_valid_id(orthologs$mgi, source_db = "mgi")
#> [1] TRUE TRUE TRUE TRUE
```

`mgi` has `pattern` mode only. A pass confirms the shape of the id. It does
not confirm that MGI holds a record for it.

## Keep mouse symbols out of the HGNC check

The `hgnc` source holds human symbols only, and biobouncer has no source for
mouse symbols. A mouse symbol is not valid in `hgnc`. When its spelling is
close to a human symbol, the suggestion is the human gene.

```{r}
res <- check_id(c("Trp53", "Kmt2a", "Nf1"), source_db = "hgnc", how = "cache")
res[c("input", "valid", "suggestion")]
```

`repair_id()` on this column would turn every mouse symbol back into a human
one. Check a mouse gene by its MGI id, as in the step above.

## Catch an answer from the wrong species

A lookup can answer for a species you did not ask for. `mygene_genes()` from
bioclients searches human genes unless `species` says otherwise. Given two
mouse symbols and no `species`, it returns the human genes.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
hits <- biohttp::body_or_null(mygene_genes(c("Trp53", "Kmt2a")))
hits[c("symbol", "ensembl_gene")]
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   symbol ensembl_gene
#>   <chr>  <chr>
#> 1 TP53   ENSG00000141510
#> 2 KMT2A  ENSG00000118058
```

An Ensembl gene id carries its species in the letters after `ENS`, so
biobouncer can test the species offline. Both ids above are well-formed
Ensembl ids, and both fail a check for mouse.

```{r}
is_valid_id(
  c("ENSG00000141510", "ENSG00000118058"),
  source_db = "ensembl",
  species = "mus_musculus"
)
```

The mouse gene id for Trp53 passes the same check.

```{r}
is_valid_id("ENSMUSG00000059552", source_db = "ensembl", species = "mus_musculus")
```

Put this check on any column of Ensembl ids that should hold one species.

## Genome assemblies

A gene symbol and an MGI id name a gene, and neither changes with the genome
assembly. Coordinates do. To test a coordinate against a build, see
[Variant identifiers](variants.html#catch-a-coordinate-from-the-wrong-genome-build).
